name: purescript
desc: Strongly typed programming language that compiles to JavaScript
why: A strongly typed Haskell-inspired language compiling to JavaScript, interesting but a mainstream-adjacent functional language.

brief.what_it_is: PureScript is a strongly typed functional programming language that compiles to JavaScript. Its source goes in and readable JavaScript comes out, so the output can run in browsers or Node and can call existing JavaScript code. The compiler executable is called purs. The language is described as small and Haskell-inspired, and it offers algebraic data types, row polymorphism, higher-kinded types, type classes with functional dependencies, and higher-rank polymorphism.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as a way to build real-world web applications, servers, and apps with functional techniques and expressive types, while compiling to readable JavaScript that can reuse existing JavaScript code. The GitHub README describes it as 'written in and inspired by Haskell.'
brief.how_it_works: The compiler, written in Haskell, takes PureScript source and emits JavaScript. Spago is the recommended build tool, and npm is recommended for managing JavaScript dependencies. The sources here did not explain the compiler internals in detail.

commands_seen.context: Installs the PureScript compiler (purs) globally through npm; the homepage notes this needs Node version 8 or later.
Installs Spago, which the homepage calls the recommended build tool for PureScript.

brief.install_notes: Precompiled binaries for OSX, Linux, and Windows are on the latest GitHub release page. The npm route needs Node 8 or later, per the homepage. Spago is recommended as the build tool, and npm handles JavaScript dependencies. No accounts or special hardware are mentioned. The homepage also links a Quick Start Guide and a try-in-browser option.
brief.standout: It targets readable JavaScript output and interop with existing JS code, while bringing a Haskell-style type system (row polymorphism, extensible records, higher-rank types) into the browser toolchain. Its own pitch leans on Haskell-style expressiveness rather than a new paradigm.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The GitHub README has a live CI badge and links to releases, a changelog, a contributing guide, a book, and community spaces. I did not find a last-release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so I cannot confirm recent activity precisely.
brief.caveats: The README calls it 'a small' language, and the homepage's npm route cites an old Node 8 minimum, which may be outdated. The language is Haskell-inspired but is not Haskell. Community discussion happens on Discord and Discourse, which the README says follow a code of conduct, and also on Matrix, StackOverflow, and IRC, which it says do not. I did not check licensing in the pages I read.
quotes: A small strongly typed programming language with expressive types that compiles to JavaScript, written in and inspired by Haskell.
Compile to readable JavaScript and reuse existing JavaScript code easily
Excellent tooling and editor support with instant rebuilds
